answer: A farm running 126 keys thus pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation trivial. Because the lantern stake is held until the inlet settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the horizon audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 18% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
